children: Bogd FT Limited, the Cayman holding company of Mongolia-based Bogd Bank JSC, filed for an initial public offering on the NYSE American under the ticker “BOGD.” The company plans to offer 6,250,000 ordinary shares at an expected price range of $4.00 to $6.00 per share, with D. Boral Capital as underwriter. Proceeds will support loan growth, technology investments, and sales channel expansion.

Bogd FT Limited is a Cayman Islands holding company whose primary operating subsidiary, Bogd Bank JSC, is a diversified Mongolian commercial bank. The bank offers retail and corporate lending, deposit products, international remittances, foreign exchange, guarantees, and insurance brokerage, and also operates an active treasury for liquidity and investment management. Its retail portfolio spans mortgages, auto, and consumer loans; corporate offerings include term loans, working capital facilities, trade finance, and supply chain solutions.

The bank serves customers through 17 branches and 8 ATMs, alongside a full-featured digital banking platform for account opening, payments, and instant lending. Bogd Bank emphasizes SME finance, rural banking, women-led enterprises, and is building green lending capabilities. Treasury activities include investments in government and corporate bonds, RMBS/ABS structures, and cross-currency hedging. Management highlights strong capital, liquidity, and asset quality metrics, along with a Moody’s BCA of b2 and long-term CRR of B1.
: Mongolia’s banking sector assets reached about MNT 85 trillion in 2025, with loans of MNT 44.2 trillion.
: Sector assets grew roughly 20% year over year in 2025; the wider sector has shown strong CAGR since 2022.
: Bogd Bank reported leading ROA (4.20%) and ROE (27.24%) among major Mongolian banks in 2025.
: Khan Bank, Golomt Bank, Khas Bank, XacBank, M Bank.
: Digitalization of financial services, rising role of foreign funding, Basel III liquidity (LCR/NSFR) adoption, and continued focus on SME and green lending.
: Focus on retail, SME, and corporate clients, including trade and agriculture segments
: 17 branches and 8 ATMs in Mongolia (as of Dec 31, 2025)
: Mortgage securitizations with MIK; SME securitizations with SFC; policy and repo programs with the Bank of Mongolia
: Total assets MNT 1.372 trillion (2025); Tier 1 capital MNT 207.05 billion; Net profit MNT 50.11 billion; LCR 212.22% and NSFR 150.01% (2025); Moody’s BCA b2 and CRR B1
: Up ~15% from MNT 64.29 billion (2024) to MNT 74.06 billion (2025)
, Chairman of the Board - Co-founder of Bodi Corporation; decades of leadership in Mongolian finance.
, Chief Executive Officer and Director - Led Bogd Bank since 2014; prior roles at Mongolia’s Ministry of Finance and Mongolian Stock Exchange.
, Chief Financial Officer - Former finance director at Mongolian Mortgage Corporation; LSE and University of Westminster graduate.
, Independent Director (effective upon effectiveness) - International executive and director; Honorary Consul of Mongolia in Luxembourg.
, Independent Director (effective upon effectiveness) - Longstanding advisor to IFC; extensive experience in Mongolia’s financial sector and public policy.
, Independent Director (effective upon effectiveness) - Managing Partner at Canmore Capital; 20 years advising on capital deployment in emerging markets.
: Approximately $25,000,000 (based on low end of range)
: ~70% to support lending (domestic and selected Central Asia markets), ~20% for technology investments, ~10% for sales channel development and expansion.
